summary: Reproduced five unreferenced fire-and-forget asyncio tasks across the three reported files. Mesh jobs now use a module-owned task set, while tokenizer-manager and multi-tokenizer work use the manager's existing asyncio_tasks set; done callbacks remove completed tasks to avoid leaks.

tests.command: AST scan of git-show output at 358c163250ad3b1f62939b01ce1314a0a31a0365 for bare *.create_task(...) expressions in the three reported files
tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: exactly five discarded task results were detected at mesh_api.py:222, multi_tokenizer_mixin.py:725, and tokenizer_manager.py:1817, 2528, and 3083. Exit 1 is the intentional regression assertion failure.

10 tests passed: no discarded task-creation expressions remain in the reported files, pending tasks are retained, successful and failed tasks are released, and existing multi-tokenizer unit behavior remains intact.
All changed Python sources compiled successfully.
The patch contains no whitespace errors.

remaining_limitations: No GPU or full model-serving run was performed because the reported defect is asyncio task ownership and is reproduced deterministically by source/lifecycle tests; no model, tensor operation, compiler, or GPU path is involved.
The prepared venv does not include ruff and PATH has no ruff, black, or isort executable; compileall, git diff --check, and focused unit tests were used instead.
